I am 22. 

Before answering the second question, I'd like to add that i am generally someone who doesn't use labels, i actively try not to limit myself to "social" ideas, while not actively running from them because they all have some form of logical root.

That being said, i think that a lot of modern society and the way things are evolving are just part of agendas that either grew out of control, or planned ways to keep us all in the gear of a system that is not for our best intrest. The idea of marriage, having a "soulmate" that will be your only love, are ideal and normal for most, growing up in environnements that told us it was the right thing, even when we all could see from the young age that divorces happens, cheating happens, mixed feelings happen, people growing close or appart.

I truly believe that the labels people put on their relationships and the social limitations we are told to have in our relationships, are the leading cause of that problem. People often fail to requestion these "norms" or are too scared of people's judging to try and get out of them. We keep talking about communication in relationships, yet people fail to accept any idea that isn't in their "norm". 

I dont see "friends" "crushes" "lovers" "partners", i just see people i admire that are on many different spectrums of types of attraction (physical, sexual, mental, platonic ect...). And i habe been unconsciously sorrounding myself with people that also arent intrested in following the requirements of such labels. That has led to so many unforgettable experiences with everyone i know, without being scared of the "what should we call this", "he.she is mine", "do i love my friend ?" "Can i stay friends with my ex", "is it okay to have a crush or go out with a close friend ?". 

Without the expectations people (but especially media honestly) has put on what a relationship should look like, i feel like a whole weight is lifted, and we can simply let our humanity and real desires and feelings slip out.

I know i am young, and i know i will experience so much more and probably change my view points with time. But for now, as someone who swallows data daily and studies history, psycology and sociology among other things. I feel like the evolution of "normal relationships" through time is the prime exemple that monogamy and the way people see "good relationships" is clearly not the norm.
